items.title: Trump halts Alzheimer's research affecting Black Americans
items.feedTitle: Scientists are fighting for their halted funds. Trust of Black communities may be harder to win back
items.summary: The Trump administration abruptly halted a study examining why Black Americans develop Alzheimer's at twice the rate of white peers, interrupting research in its final stages. The move raises concerns about trust in Black communities toward federal health research. Scientists are advocating to resume the work and rebuild community confidence in medical institutions.

items.title: FBI investigates hack of national criminal justice database
items.feedTitle: AP source: FBI investigating apparent hack of its key national criminal justice database
items.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a critical database used by federal, state, and local law enforcement. The NCIC contains records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history, and stolen property. The scope and impact of the breach remain under investigation.

items.title: Army plans lead azide detonation despite court pause order
items.feedTitle: Army plans to proceed with lead azide detonation despite indefinite pause
items.summary: The U.S. Army says it will proceed with a controlled detonation of lead azide explosive material despite a federal court's indefinite pause order. The Army invoked an emergency munitions exclusion, citing public safety concerns. The move is being contested in court filings.

items.title: AI detects system flaws, risks triggering more tech outages
items.feedTitle: As AI detects flaws in computer systems, is it causing more tech outages and disruptions?
items.summary: As AI systems rapidly identify vulnerabilities in computer infrastructure, companies face pressure to fix them quickly, potentially leading to unintended consequences like service disruptions. Experts warn the rush to patch issues flagged by AI could cause cascading failures. The trend reflects a double-edged sword in tech modernization.

items.title: Trump proposes capping credit card interest rates at 10 percent
items.feedTitle: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
items.summary: President Trump said he would work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent, a substantial reduction from the current median of roughly 22.2 percent. The proposal aims to reduce the burden on consumers but would significantly constrain credit card companies' revenue. Details on implementation remain unclear.

stlouis.title: Missouri illegal slot machines still entering gas stations
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri AG barred illegal slot machines. They're still going back into gas stations.
stlouis.summary: Despite Missouri's attorney general barring illegal slot machines, the devices continue being installed in gas stations across the state. The enforcement action appears ineffective in stopping the practice. The issue highlights a gap between regulation and compliance in the gaming sector.

stlouis.title: MetroLink transit opens to MidAmerica on November 30
stlouis.summary: St. Louis MetroLink expanded its service to reach MidAmerica Airport on November 30, extending the region's public transit connectivity. The expansion was aimed at improving airport access for residents and workers in the metro area.

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse over fossil fuel disagreement

items.summary: The United Nations climate summit in Turkey ended without consensus as nations clashed over fossil fuel language in the final agreement. The EU, UK, and developing nations rejected a draft that failed to explicitly mention moving away from fossil fuels. The impasse reflects deep divisions on how to accelerate climate action.

items.title: Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes on Kyiv

items.summary: Russian military strikes on Ukraine's Kyiv region caused a residential building to collapse, leaving residents searching for missing persons. items.title: Mexican cartel leader El Chapo Isidro arrested in gunfight
items.feedTitle: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro and one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, was arrested following a shootout with Mexican security forces in Sinaloa state. He had led the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later his own criminal organization. The operation triggered violence in the region.

items.title: Claude AI helped mathematician prove century-old math problem
items.feedTitle: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
items.summary: A mathematician at Anthropic says the company's Claude AI tool helped him solve the 19th-century Riemann hypothesis in roughly six weeks. Two groups have verified the mathematician's claim, though formal verification is ongoing. The achievement highlights AI's emerging role in mathematical research.

items.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages, raid homes and vehicles
items.feedTitle: Netanyahu rival condemns ‘Jewish terrorism’ after settler attacks on Palestinian villages
items.summary: Dozens of militant Israeli settlers raided Palestinian towns and villages in the occupied West Bank on Saturday night, setting fires to vehicles and homes. The attacks drew political condemnation within Israel, including from opposition figures. No deaths were immediately reported but property damage was extensive.

items.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri water brand

items.summary: India's food regulator (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after water samples failed safety tests twice, with findings of non-compliant bromate limits. The regulator declared the product unsafe under food safety law. The action raises concerns about packaged drinking water quality oversight.

items.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives for first India visit
items.feedTitle: Nepal PM Balen Shah kicks off India visit with EAM Jaishankar meeting; connectivity, trade, energy in focus ahead of talks with PM Modi
items.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in Delhi for his first official visit to India, meeting with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. The talks focus on energy, connectivity, infrastructure, and trade to boost bilateral ties. The visit signals strengthening India-Nepal relations under the new Nepalese government.

items.title: India and China hold talks to ease border tensions

items.summary: India and China held ten-day talks focusing on establishing engagement protocols and preventing face-offs along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh. The discussions aimed to maintain open communication and reduce misunderstandings between troops. The talks represent diplomatic efforts to stabilize the disputed border.

items.title: Jammu Kashmir recruitment board cheating case widens
items.feedTitle: Twenty held in Jammu and Kashmir recruitment board cheating case; ‘no paper leak found’
items.summary: Police arrested twenty people in a recruitment board cheating scheme involving government employees, candidates, and intermediaries who allegedly facilitated exam fraud using electronic devices. The investigation exposed an organized network operating within the system. Additional arrests include government officials implicated in the scheme.

items.title: Hyderabad police alert after terror threat email received
items.feedTitle: Hyderabad Police issue alert over terror threat email; security checks conducted at key locations
items.summary: Hyderabad Police issued an alert following a bomb threat email and conducted security checks at key locations throughout the city. The nature and credibility of the threat remain under investigation. Additional security measures were deployed in response to the warning.

immigration.title: Labor Department proposes stricter PERM green card rules
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor proposed sweeping changes to the PERM (Permanent Labor Certification) program for employment-based green cards, including 90-day recruitment periods and a 2-year layoff bar. The proposal would end Schedule A expedited processing for certain occupations including nurses. Status: Proposed, not final; comment period in progress. Affects Indian workers in STEM, healthcare, and professional roles seeking permanent residency.

immigration.title: H-1B visa workers leaving US amid policy uncertainty
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B Visa Workers Are Fed Up and Abandoning American Tech Jobs
immigration.summary: Rising numbers of H-1B visa workers are departing the United States as Trump administration policies and visa delays push them toward UK and global alternatives. Tech companies have reduced H-1B sponsorships, with issuances dropping significantly. Status: Ongoing trend, finalized policy direction under Trump. The exodus reflects frustration with visa processing delays and uncertain work authorization renewals.

immigration.title: Labor Department would end nurse green card fast-track
immigration.feedTitle: Nurse Green Card Fast Track Would End Under Labor Department Proposal
immigration.summary: The Trump administration's Labor Department proposal would eliminate the Schedule A expedited green card pathway for foreign nurses and other healthcare professionals facing documented shortages. Hospitals warn eliminating the fast-track will worsen staffing shortages. Status: Proposed rule, not finalized; part of broader PERM overhaul affecting visa sponsorship timelines.

items.feedTitle: U.S. Stocks Extend Plunge as AI Boom Turns to Bust
items.summary: U.S. stock markets extended a sharp decline as the AI investment thesis faced mounting skepticism. items.summary: Copper prices fell sharply amid broader metals market volatility, raising concerns about global economic growth and AI infrastructure buildout. cards.title: Start with identity, not goals
cards.insight: Research on habit formation shows people who frame behavior change around identity ("I am disciplined," "I am a runner") sustain change longer than those chasing external goals ("I want to lose 10 pounds"). When you anchor a new habit to who you want to be, compliance becomes self-reinforcing rather than willpower-dependent.
cards.takeaway: Pick one new habit and define it as a core identity trait, then perform that action daily for two weeks before evaluating.

cards.title: Stack habits to anchor them in routine
cards.insight: Existing routines are the most reliable triggers for new behaviors. Pairing a new habit immediately after a well-established one (e.g., meditation after morning coffee) reduces the cognitive load of remembering and creates automatic sequencing. The old habit becomes a cue.
cards.takeaway: Identify one strong daily habit you already own, and immediately follow it with your target behavior for 21 days.

cards.title: Make failure cost-free in the first month
cards.insight: Perfectionism kills habit adoption. Skipping once often cascades to abandonment because people interpret one miss as evidence the habit "isn't for me." Building in explicit permission for one missed day per week in the early phase removes the shame and self-judgment that derail commitment.
cards.takeaway: Plan two "grace days" each week where you skip guilt-free; treat the other five as non-negotiable.

cards.title: Measure the wrong thing and lose momentum
cards.insight: Outcomes (weight, fitness, savings balance) take weeks to shift; effort metrics (days completed, consistency score, time invested) shift immediately and sustain motivation. Early wins on effort reinforce the loop before outcome payoffs arrive, preventing dropout at the vulnerable weeks-2-to-4 window.
cards.takeaway: Track completion percentage, not results, for the first month; celebrate hitting your effort target, not the scale.

ai.title: China ran covert spy operation for US AI chips
ai.feedTitle: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
ai.summary: U.S. intelligence reports that China's spy agencies conducted a two-year campaign to acquire advanced U.S. AI chips, bypassing export controls imposed on companies like Nvidia. The operation highlights the strategic importance of semiconductor access to AI development. Intelligence officials warned the breach undermines U.S. efforts to restrict China's AI capabilities.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO marks largest in startup history
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic had the largest IPO ever. What does that mean for their future — and ours?
ai.summary: Anthropic completed the largest IPO ever for a startup, raising approximately $5.3 billion and valuing the AI company at $180 billion. The offering used an unconventional process similar to SpaceX that some Wall Street bankers found frustrating. The IPO comes as investor enthusiasm for AI faces intense scrutiny following a market correction.

ai.title: OpenAI chief proposes shared AI development limits framework
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI chief scientist proposes shared AI development limits tied to prediction scores
ai.summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Dario Amodei proposed using prediction scores as a basis for shared development limits on frontier AI systems. The framework aims to coordinate safety standards across AI companies without regulatory mandates. The proposal reflects growing concerns about uncontrolled AI capability scaling.

ai.title: Etsy faces backlash over AI model training in policy
ai.feedTitle: Etsy faces backlash over including AI model training in new policy update
ai.summary: E-commerce platform Etsy faced user backlash after including AI model training in its updated terms of service, allowing the company to use seller content for training data. The policy sparked concerns among creators about unauthorized use of their work. The controversy reflects broader tensions between AI development and creator rights.

ai.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model for users
ai.feedTitle: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model, rivals Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
ai.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a new AI model positioned to compete with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol in performance benchmarks.
